changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For operational buyers (COO, ops leads) at merchants whose revenue comes in spikes, such as on-sales: "A name, not a queue." Lead with the named people the customer will have, such as a solutions engineer and an account lead, and the escalation path they call during a live failure. Do not lead with tiers or response times. Only name coverage commitments our solutions engineering team has confirmed we can staff.
changes.why: When the decider asked "who's my person" and got the support plans, she called them "a queue with a faster timer", so the tiered-response framing described the ticket-form problem she was trying to escape.

changes.change: For merchants with scheduled peak events: add an "on-sale morning" coverage plan as a proof asset. It should show, on paper, who is watching, who the customer calls, and what we do in the first minutes after payments start failing. Build it with our solutions engineer for each deal until it exists as a standard offering, and include only commitments we have confirmed internally.
changes.why: The decider wanted to see on paper what we do on an on-sale morning, and the rep said "We don't have that as a thing" even though he could have built it with our solutions engineer.

changes.change: Opening line for operational buyers at spike-driven merchants, used in place of the global-growth opener and uptime statistics: frame the pitch around what happens in the first minutes of a live failure, in the customer's words: "I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down." Make this pitch directly to the operational decider, not through the technical champion.
changes.why: The deal was triggered by a live failure where support replied only after the on-sale was over, and the decider who made the call in one meeting rejected uptime as the thing she buys while our technical proof reached her only secondhand.

changes.change: Proof point alongside customer stories for operational buyers: offer a reference person who can describe how we responded during a live spike or incident, not just a logo.
changes.why: The rep said "I had logos. I didn't have a person." to a buyer whose test was "A name, not a queue."
